epithet: Glory be to Him who took His servant by night
lede: One night, in the hardest stretch of his life, the Prophet ﷺ was taken from the mosque at Makkah to the farthest mosque in Jerusalem, and shown some of the signs of his Lord. The surah gives that journey a single ayah. The rest is what he came back with: a Qurʾan that “guides to what is most upright”, and the commandments to live by it.

names.name: al-Isrāʾ
names.note: After the journey by night told in its first ayah.

names.name: Banī Isrāʾīl
names.note: The name by which the Companions knew it — Ibn Masʿūd and ʿĀʾishah both call it this — after the account of the Children of Israel that follows the opening (17:2–8).

revelation.detail: Ibn al-Jawzī says it is Makkan in the saying of the generality, though some held that parts are Madinan: a report from Ibn ʿAbbās, followed by Qatādah, sets apart eight ayat beginning “They were about to tempt you away” (17:73), and al-Qurṭubī names three. Ibn Masʿūd counted it with al-Kahf and Maryam among the earliest surahs he had learned. Its opening fixes it after the Night Journey, which took place in the last years before the Hijrah. The traditional order places it fiftieth.
revelation.when: Makkah, after the Night Journey — the last years before the Hijrah{?The reports of when the Night Journey took place differ by years. About a year before the Hijrah is the saying most often given; Ibn Isḥāq tells of the Journey before the deaths of Khadījah and Abū Ṭālib.}

evidence.quote: هِيَ مَكِّيَّةٌ في قَوْلِ الجَماعَةِ، إلّا أنَّ بَعْضَهم يَقُولُ: فِيها مَدَنِيٌّ
سَمِعْتُ ابْنَ مَسْعُودٍ، رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ، قَالَ فِي بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ وَالْكَهْفِ وَمَرْيَمَ: إِنَّهُنَّ مِنَ الْعِتَاقِ الْأُوَلِ وَهُنَّ مِنْ تِلَادِي
هَذِهِ السُّورَةُ مَكِّيَّةٌ، إِلَّا ثَلَاثَ آيَاتٍ

attested.quote: سُورَةُ الْإِسْرَاءِ مَكِّيَّةٌ وَهِيَ مِائَةٌ وَإِحْدَى عَشْرَةَ آيَةً
أخْرَجَ النَّحّاسُ، وابْنُ مَرْدُويَهْ، عَنِ اِبْنِ عَبّاسٍ قالَ: نَزَلَتْ سُورَةُ ”بَنِي إسْرائِيلَ“ بِمَكَّةَ
attested.says: Ibn ʿAbbās: it came down in Makkah. Recorded by al-Naḥḥās and Ibn Mardawayh.

setting: By the dating most widely held, it was about a year before the Hijrah{?The reports of when the Night Journey took place differ by years. About a year before the Hijrah is the saying most often given; Ibn Isḥāq tells of the Journey before the deaths of Khadījah and Abū Ṭālib.}: Khadījah was dead, and Abū Ṭālib, and al-Ṭāʾif had driven him out with stones. The Prophet ﷺ was brought a mount called al-Burāq, and carried by night to Jerusalem, where he prayed, and from there taken up through the heavens. When he told Quraysh in the morning, they laughed; and ʿĀʾishah relates that some who had believed fell away.{?al-Albānī includes this report in al-Silsilah al-Ṣaḥīḥah (306), as an index of his works records it; it has not yet been checked here against the printed book. Other scholars fault its chain.} The surah refers to that test in its sixtieth ayah — “We did not make the vision We showed you except as a trial for people” — and Ibn ʿAbbās explains: it was a vision of the eye, shown to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the night he was taken to Jerusalem.

What is striking is how little the surah says about it. One ayah, beginning with a word of awe — Subḥān — and calling him by the highest title he has: “His servant.” Then, without a pause, it turns to Mūsā, the Book given to him, and the people who received it — who twice spread corruption in the land and were twice overrun, their Temple entered and laid waste. The sanctuary to which he had just been carried had been lost by its keepers. The next ayah says why this is being told: “This Qurʾan guides to what is most upright.” Another people are about to be entrusted.

And so the surah gives them their charge. In seventeen ayat (17:23–39) it sets out a whole way of life, opening and closing with the oneness of Allah. Worship none but Him. Be good to parents — “do not say to them so much as ‘uff’… and lower to them the wing of humility, out of mercy, and say: My Lord, have mercy on them, as they raised me when I was small.” Give the kinsman his due. Do not squander, and do not be tight-fisted. Do not kill your children for fear of want. Do not go near adultery. Do not take life. Do not touch the orphan’s property. Keep your word. Give full measure. Do not pursue what you have no knowledge of. Do not walk the earth exultantly. “That is part of the wisdom your Lord has revealed to you.”

Few surahs speak of the Qurʾan by name so insistently. It is a healing and a mercy. If mankind and jinn joined forces to produce its like, they could not. It was sent down in truth and in truth it descended, in portions, to be recited to people at intervals. Quraysh, for their part, set out what it would take to convince them — a spring gushing from the ground, a garden, the sky brought down in pieces, a house of gold, a ladder to heaven and a book fetched down from it — and are answered in one line: “Say: glory be to my Lord! Am I anything but a human being, a messenger?”

There is pressure in it, plainly stated: “They were about to tempt you away from what We revealed to you… and had We not made you firm, you would almost have inclined to them a little.” “They were about to scare you out of the land.” And there is the answer to the pressure: the prayer from the sun’s decline to the dark of night, the recitation at dawn, the night vigil — “it may be that your Lord will raise you to a praised station” — and a prayer of his own: “My Lord, bring me in by an entrance of truth, and bring me out by an exit of truth.” Then: “Say: the truth has come, and falsehood has vanished.” Within ten years he would say those words aloud, in Makkah, to three hundred and sixty idols.

occasions.title: The Night Journey, as he ﷺ told it
occasions.text: Anas ibn Mālik relates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I was brought al-Burāq — a white animal, long, larger than a donkey and smaller than a mule, which sets its hoof at the furthest point its eye can reach. I rode it until I came to Jerusalem, and I tethered it at the ring where the prophets tether their mounts. Then I entered the mosque and prayed two rakʿahs in it, and came out; and Jibrīl brought me a vessel of wine and a vessel of milk. I chose the milk, and Jibrīl said: You have chosen the natural way.”
story: Then he was taken up. At each heaven Jibrīl asked for it to be opened, and was asked: “Who are you?” — “Jibrīl.” — “And who is with you?” — “Muḥammad.” — “Has he been sent for?” — “He has been sent for.” In the first heaven he met Ādam, who welcomed him and prayed for good for him. In the second were the two cousins, ʿĪsā son of Maryam and Yaḥyā son of Zakariyyā; in the third Yūsuf, “who had been given half of all beauty”; in the fourth Idrīs, of whom Allah says, “We raised him to a high place”; in the fifth Hārūn; in the sixth Mūsā. In the seventh was Ibrāhīm, resting his back against the Much-Frequented House, which seventy thousand angels enter each day and do not return to again.

“Then I was taken to the Lote Tree of the Furthest Limit. Its leaves were like the ears of elephants and its fruits like great jars. And when there covered it, by the command of Allah, what covered it, it was changed, and no one of Allah’s creation could describe it for its beauty.” There Allah revealed to him what He revealed, and made fifty prayers obligatory in every day and night.

On the way down he came to Mūsā, who asked: “What has your Lord enjoined upon your community?” — “Fifty prayers.” — “Go back to your Lord and ask Him to lighten it. Your community cannot bear that; I have tried the Children of Israel and tested them.” He went back and said, “My Lord, lighten it for my community,” and five were taken off; and Mūsā said the same again. “I did not cease going back and forth between my Lord and Mūsā until He said: Muḥammad, they are five prayers in every day and night, and each prayer is as ten; that is fifty prayers. Whoever intends a good deed and does not do it, one good deed is written for him, and if he does it, ten are written; and whoever intends an evil deed and does not do it, nothing is written, and if he does it, one evil deed is written.” When he told Mūsā, he said once more: go back and ask for it to be lightened. “I said: I have gone back to my Lord until I am ashamed before Him.”
occasions.source: Anas ibn Mālik: Muslim (162). Al-Bukhārī gives the ascent from Mālik ibn Ṣaʿṣaʿah (3887).

occasions.title: “They ask you about the spirit”
occasions.text: Quraysh said to the Jews: “Give us something to ask this man about.” They said: “Ask him about the spirit.” So they asked him, and Allah sent down: “They ask you about the spirit. Say: the spirit is of the command of my Lord; and you have been given of knowledge only a little.”
occasions.source: Ibn ʿAbbās: al-Tirmidhī (3140); a ṣaḥīḥ chain according to al-Albānī. Ibn Masʿūd relates the question from a group of Jews in Madinah: al-Bukhārī (4721) and Muslim (2794).

occasions.title: Neither loud nor silent
occasions.text: “It came down while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in hiding in Makkah. When he prayed with his Companions he would raise his voice with the Qurʾan; and when the idolaters heard it, they reviled the Qurʾan, and Him who sent it down, and him who brought it. So Allah said to His Prophet ﷺ: ‘Do not be loud in your prayer’ — so that the idolaters hear and revile the Qurʾan — ‘nor silent in it’ — so that your Companions cannot hear — ‘but seek a way between.’”

aim: To set out the perfection of the message of Muḥammad ﷺ; in it are signs and good tidings for that message, in what it contains and in what was to come.
themes: The two corruptions of the Children of Israel
The Qurʾan guides to what is most upright
The honour of the children of Ādam
The prayers, and the praised station

outline.title: The journey, and the first trustees
outline.summary: Glory be to Him who took His servant by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque, whose surroundings We have blessed, to show him some of Our signs. We gave Mūsā the Book, and made it a guidance for the Children of Israel. We decreed for the Children of Israel in the Book: you will spread corruption in the land twice. When the first of the two came, We sent against you servants of Ours of great might. Then We gave you back your turn. If you do good, you do good for yourselves; and if you return, We return.

outline.title: What is most upright
outline.summary: This Qurʾan guides to what is most upright (17:9). Man prays for evil as he prays for good; man is ever hasty. We have fastened every person’s fate to his neck, and on the Day of Resurrection We shall bring out for him a book he will find spread open: “Read your book; today you are enough as a reckoner against yourself.” No bearer of burdens bears the burden of another; and We do not punish until We have sent a messenger. Whoever desires the fleeting life — and whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it as it should be striven for.

outline.title: The commandments
outline.summary: Your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, and that you be good to parents: do not say to them “uff”; lower to them the wing of humility, out of mercy. Give the kinsman his due, and the needy, and the traveller; do not squander. Do not kill your children for fear of poverty. Do not go near adultery. Do not take the life Allah has made sacred. Do not approach the orphan’s property. Fulfil the covenant. Give full measure. Do not pursue what you have no knowledge of. Do not walk the earth exultantly. That is part of the wisdom your Lord has revealed to you.

outline.title: The Qurʾan, and those who turn from it
outline.summary: We have set things out in this Qurʾan in many ways, that they may take heed. The seven heavens and the earth and whoever is in them glorify Him; there is not a thing but glorifies Him with praise, though you do not understand their glorifying. They say: “When we are bones and fragments, shall we be raised?” Tell My servants to say what is best. Those they call upon are themselves seeking a way to their Lord. We did not make the vision We showed you except as a trial for people.

outline.title: Iblīs, and the honour of mankind
outline.summary: When We said to the angels, “Prostrate to Ādam” — Iblīs said: “Shall I prostrate to one You created of clay? If You give me respite, I shall master his descendants, all but a few.” — “Over My servants you have no authority.” Your Lord is He who drives the ship for you through the sea. We have honoured the children of Ādam, carried them on land and sea, and preferred them above many of those We created. The Day We call every people with their leader.

outline.title: Held firm
outline.summary: They were about to tempt you away from what We revealed to you; had We not made you firm, you would almost have inclined to them a little. Establish the prayer from the decline of the sun to the darkness of the night, and the recitation of dawn: the recitation of dawn is witnessed. And in part of the night, keep vigil with it; it may be that your Lord will raise you to a praised station. Say: “My Lord, bring me in by an entrance of truth.” Say: the truth has come, and falsehood has vanished. We send down of the Qurʾan what is a healing and a mercy for the believers.

outline.title: The spirit, the challenge, and their demands
outline.summary: They ask you about the spirit. Say: the spirit is of the command of my Lord. Say: if mankind and jinn gathered to produce the like of this Qurʾan, they could not produce its like. They say: “We shall not believe you until you make a spring gush from the earth for us… or you ascend into heaven.” Say: glory be to my Lord! Am I anything but a human being, a messenger? Nothing kept people from believing but that they said, “Has Allah sent a human being as messenger?”

outline.title: The close
outline.summary: We gave Mūsā nine clear signs. With the truth We sent it down, and with the truth it has come down. A Qurʾan We have divided, that you may recite it to people at intervals. Those given knowledge before it, when it is recited to them, fall on their faces in prostration, weeping, and it increases them in humility. Say: call upon Allah, or call upon the Most Merciful; whichever you call — His are the Most Beautiful Names. And say: “Praise be to Allah, who has taken no son, and has no partner in sovereignty.”

keyAyah.why: The sentence on which the surah turns — from the people who lost the trust to the Book that carries it now.

virtues.text: ʿĀʾishah said: “The Prophet ﷺ would not sleep until he had recited Banī Isrāʾīl and al-Zumar.”
virtues.arabic: كَانَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم لاَ يَنَامُ حَتَّى يَقْرَأَ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ وَالزُّمَرَ

virtues.text: Ibn Masʿūd said of Banī Isrāʾīl, al-Kahf and Maryam: “They are among the first and finest, and they are my oldest wealth.”
virtues.arabic: إِنَّهُنَّ مِنَ الْعِتَاقِ الأُوَلِ وَهُنَّ مِنْ تِلاَدِي

virtues.text: The Prophet ﷺ entered Makkah, and around the House were three hundred and sixty idols. He began to strike them with a stick in his hand, saying: “The truth has come, and falsehood has vanished. The truth has come, and falsehood neither begins anything nor brings it back.”

Ibn ʿUmar said: “On the Day of Resurrection people will be on their knees, each community following its prophet, saying: ‘So-and-so, intercede!’ — until the intercession comes to the Prophet ﷺ. That is the day on which Allah will raise him to the praised station.”

“The prayer in congregation is twenty-five degrees better than the prayer of one alone; and the angels of the night and the angels of the day gather at the dawn prayer.” Abū Hurayrah said: recite, if you wish: “The recitation of dawn is witnessed.”

virtuesNote: The hundred and ninth ayah is an ayah of prostration.
before: Al-Naḥl ended by telling the Prophet ﷺ to be patient, and that Allah is with the mindful. Al-Isrāʾ opens with how near: a journey by night to His signs.
after: Al-Isrāʾ opens with glorification and ends with praise: “Praise be to Allah, who has taken no son.” Al-Kahf opens: “Praise be to Allah, who sent down the Book upon His servant.”
